# Test Framework Scaffolder

**One-stop scaffolder for Playwright functional automation and k6 performance testing.**

`test-framework-scaffolder` is an interactive, composable CLI generator for Playwright projects in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Java, plus k6 performance projects with Grafana dashboards. It supports BDD or TDD/Non-BDD styles, focused UI/API automation, reusable app fixtures, Java with JUnit 5 or TestNG, configurable k6 load profiles, thresholds, Prometheus, and Grafana.

[Open the complete illustrated installation and user guide](https://unpkg.com/test-framework-scaffolder@latest/docs/user-guide.html) for prompt choices, configuration, execution commands, reporting, CI, and troubleshooting.

## Installation and quick start

The easiest option is to run the latest published version without installing it globally:

```bash
mkdir my-automation-projects
cd my-automation-projects
npx test-framework-scaffolder@latest
```

The CLI asks for the project name, language, BDD or Non-BDD style, framework options, and dependency installation. It prints the exact generated location and next commands when finished.

For an optional global installation:

```bash
npm install --global test-framework-scaffolder@latest
test-framework-scaffolder
```

## Requirements

Node.js 22 or newer is required. Generated Python, Java, or k6 projects also require their respective runtime; Docker Compose is needed only for the local Grafana dashboard.

## Local development

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm link
test-framework-scaffolder
```

Run the unpublished local build without linking:

```bash
node dist/cli/index.js
```

The prompts choose project name, framework style, test type, Allure, GitHub Actions, and automatic dependency installation. Every project includes smoke and UAT data; runtime selection is centralized in `config/run.config.json` rather than asked during generation.

Language choices are TypeScript, JavaScript, Python with pytest, Java with Maven, and Performance with k6 + Grafana. BDD uses `playwright-bdd` for TypeScript/JavaScript, `pytest-bdd` for Python, Cucumber with either JUnit Platform or TestNG for Java, and a lightweight Given/When/Then specification and step layer for native k6 execution.

For a generated performance project, start Prometheus and Grafana and run the default profile with:

```bash
docker compose up -d
npm run test:grafana
```

Change `environment` or `profile` in `config/run.config.json`; any matching `test-data/<environment>.json` is loaded automatically. Override them temporarily with `npm test -- --env uat --profile load`.

## Generator architecture

```text
src/
├── cli/                 prompts, presentation, process orchestration
├── generators/          conditional project composition
├── utils/               validation and filesystem utilities
├── templates/
│   ├── common/          config, fixtures, data, scripts, docs
│   ├── bdd/             Gherkin, steps, playwright-bdd config
│   ├── non-bdd/         standard Playwright specs
│   ├── ui/              Page Object layer
│   ├── api/             request/client/service/model/validator layers
│   ├── allure/          runtime metadata
│   └── github/          CI workflow
└── types.ts
```

Templates are copied and composed based on the selected capabilities; unused test layers are removed. Placeholder substitution is limited to configuration values and small conditional source fragments—project files remain individually maintainable templates.

## Development

```bash
npm run build
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm test
npm run format:check
```

Generator tests create all BDD/non-BDD × UI/API/UI+API combinations plus both k6 styles in temporary directories and assert inclusion/exclusion rules. See the README generated inside each project for framework commands, architecture, test data, observability, Allure, and CI guidance.

## Publishing

Run the quality checks and preview the package before publishing: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, and `npm pack --dry-run`. npm package names are lowercase, so the registry name is `test-framework-scaffolder`; the product title is **Test Framework Scaffolder**.
